name: typeahead-suggestions

assert_screen: contains:/help  Show help and keyboard shortcuts

notes: The typeahead popup is chunk[4] of the render_app layout — a separately budgeted row group that vanishes silently when suggestions go empty, taking the input's vertical position with it. ENV: the ORDER of the rows comes from ~/.operant/slash-usage.json (recency then frequency), so the text baseline is machine-specific; Post-cutover (iter-655): the ported chrome draws suggestions as `cmd  description` with no `[cmd]` badge; assert_screen checks a full description string, which fails if the description wiring drops to empty (it did — the TuiState seam returned &'static str and the adapter shipped ""). (iter-1787) The note that used to sit here said "two-or-more-character prefixes ('/sk', '/he', '/ex') currently paint zero rows while single-character prefixes do — a real inconsistency worth a follow-up". MEASURED 2026-11-06 against the corpus's own pinned environment at both corpus sizes (120x40 and 80x24): the claim is FALSE. '/sk' paints the /skills row, '/he' paints the /help row, '/ex' paints the /exit row — the popup paints its rows for every prefix, one character or more. The note named a defect that does not exist, which is the expensive half: the next reader would have gone hunting in working code (or "fixed" the typeahead into a regression). The 100x30 variant is the PIN: it types a two-character prefix and asserts the matching row is painted, so the note cannot go stale silently again.
